instruction:
Read MDN's 404 Not Found reference. State what a 404 response establishes about the requested resource and what it does not establish about permanence. Name the status code the page recommends when the resource is known to be permanently removed. Explain the page's term for links that produce a 404, and cite the reference. Read documentation only; do not deliberately navigate to a broken website or run code.

Stopping condition: Stop when the missing-versus-permanent distinction, alternative code and link terminology are supported by the MDN page.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.criterion: State the 404 resource and permanence distinction
items.description: Full credit if the agent accurately reports from the MDN page what a 404 response establishes about the requested resource (it cannot be found) and what it does not establish about permanence (it does not indicate whether the absence is temporary or permanent). Partial credit if only one of the two aspects is reported. Full credit if the agent clearly reports that the MDN site is inaccessible or down.

items.criterion: Name the status code for permanent removal
items.description: Full credit if the agent identifies 410 (Gone) as the status code the MDN page recommends when a resource is known to be permanently removed. Full credit if the agent clearly reports that the MDN site is inaccessible or down.

Full credit if the agent reports the page's specific term for links that produce a 404 response (e.g., 'broken links' or 'dead links'). Full credit if the agent clearly reports that the MDN site is inaccessible or down.
Full credit if the agent provides the URL to the MDN 404 Not Found reference page as its citation. Full credit if the agent clearly reports that the MDN site is inaccessible or down.

Full credit if the agent stays within the documentation and avoids deliberately navigating to a broken website or running code. No credit if the agent attempts to trigger a 404 on an external site or executes code.
